sentences.text:
In Re:- Radhanath Mondal vs Re: An Application For Bail Under
... on 15 March, 2016
Author: Ashim Kumar Roy
Bench: Ashim Kumar Roy
 1
32 15.3.2016
pd. C.R.M. No. 2058 of 2016
 In re:- Radhanath Mondal ... Petitioner.

-And- 
Re: An application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. affirmed on 9.3.2016 in connection with
Moyna Police Station Case No.228/2015 dated 28.9.2015 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860 read with West Bengal Act 42 of 1973 and Sections 3/304/120B of the Indian
Penal Code. 1860 and Section 46Aa of the Bengal Excise Act 1909 and Section 16(3) of the
Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954.

Mr. Deep Chaim Kabir, Mr. Mazhar Hossain Chowdhury
...
For the petitioner.
Mr. Binoy Kumar Panda .... For the State.

Leave is given to the learned Counsel for the petitioner to make necessary correction in the cause
title of this application for bail.
Heard the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the parties.
Perused the Case Diary.
The petitioner is in custody for six months.
Till date, charge has not been framed.
According to the case of the prosecution, total 28 persons died by consuming spurious and poisonous country liquor.
However, it is an admitted position that only in respect of ten persons,
post mortem
was held and so far as the balance eighteen persons are concerned, they were cremated without any post mortem
. The F.S.L. Report of the victim also supports the prosecution case.
Now, the prayer for bail of the petitioner has been opposed from the side of the State by referring the statements of the witnesses, which are at pages 19 and 20 of the Case Diary.

sentences.text: It appears that although according to the aforesaid witnesses, one Dulal Bisui and Manik Ruidas are the principal accused and from their possession, huge quantity of poisonous I.D. Liquor was seized but from the possession of the present petitioner, only a two litres bottle containing one litre of such I.D. Liquor was recovered and on examination of the same, it was found to have contain poisonous element.
The learned Counsel for the petitioner, in his usual fairness, contends that the petitioner was possessing the said I.D.Liquor for his own consumption.

Now, considering the role attributed to the petitioner in the commission of the offence and more particularly the quantity of I.D. Liquor alleged to have been seized from the possession of the petitioner, we are of the opinion that the prayer for bail of the petitioner may be considered favourably, although the date for framing of charge has been fixed on March 17, 2016.
Accordingly, we allow the petitioner's prayer for bail.

Let the petitioner be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.30,000/- with two sureties of Rs.15,000/- each, one of whom must be local,
to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Purba Medinipur subject to the further condition that after release, the petitioner shall not enter within the jurisdiction of Moyna Police Station or within the area, which is situated surrounding the Moyna Police Station, except for the purpose of attending the court's proceedings and he shall report to the Officer-in-Charge of the concerned Police Station, where he shall reside after release, thrice in every week, until further orders.

We make it clear that if the petitioner fails to make himself available before the trial court on any day fixed for trial without any sufficient reason and due to the reason beyond his control, the learned trial court shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the petitioner and take him into custody without any further reference to this Court.
The application for bail is, thus, disposed of.

(Ashim Kumar Roy, J.) (C. S. Karnan, J.)
